about: The comparison behind the choice of embedding model for embeddings_bge_m3: two open models and a baseline with no model, run with the same benchmark on the same text. Figures copied from the benchmark's result files.

run.script: the same retrieval benchmark for every model (tasks below)
run.text: the kural text of 2026-10-17, before the last text rulings; the vectors shipped in embeddings_bge_m3 were computed again on the final text (embeddings_bge_m3.json)
run.queries: 1,330 for each task but misquote, which had 1,280: the misquote queries come from the reading atlas as it stood then. The atlas grows as rulings reject readings, so the shipped vectors' benchmark (embeddings_bge_m3.json) has more.

tasks: A kural in Tamil finds Pope's English translation of it first
Pope's English finds the Tamil kural first
Drew and Lazarus's English finds Pope's English for the same kural first
A variant reading of a kural finds the right kural first

runs.label: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
runs.settings: query prompt: the model's own query instruction
runs.revision_note: as reported by the benchmark run

runs.label: No model (letter trigrams)
runs.settings: no model: the letter trigrams of each text, spaces removed, hashed into 4,096 counts; float32 cosines, so where cosines tie the order can differ from the exact baseline in embeddings_bge_m3.json

bge_m3_model_card.read_from: the model's Hugging Face snapshot at the revision below

quotes.functionality: Multi-Functionality: It can simultaneously perform the three common retrieval functionalities of embedding model: dense retrieval, multi-vector retrieval, and sparse retrieval.
quotes.languages: Multi-Linguality: It can support more than 100 working languages.
quotes.length: Multi-Granularity: It is able to process inputs of different granularities, spanning from short sentences to long documents of up to 8192 tokens.

bge_m3_model_card.tamil: not named anywhere in the card; it says only 'more than 100 working languages'
bge_m3_model_card.used_here: the dense vectors only (sentence-transformers, normalised, 1,024 numbers per text); not the multi-vector or sparse outputs
